== Biography ==

Cotton-tail is one of four young rabbits living with their Mother in a sand-bank, underneath the root of a very big fir-tree. Cotton-tail belongs to a family of well-behaved rabbits, and is characterized by obedience and propriety.

When their Mother ventures out to the baker's, Cotton-tail proves a dutiful child. After purchasing a loaf of brown bread and five currant buns, Mother Rabbit instructs her young ones, and Cotton-tail, along with siblings Flopsy and Mopsy, dutifully obeys. The three "good little bunnies" proceed down the lane to gather blackberries, demonstrating the orderly conduct their Mother has instilled.

Following the day's events—during which their sibling Peter ventures recklessly into Mr. McGregor's garden and incurs their Mother's displeasure—Cotton-tail enjoys a proper supper of bread and milk alongside the blackberries gathered earlier, a fitting reward for good behavior.

== Narrative role ==

Cotton-tail is one of four young rabbits dwelling with their mother in a sand-bank beneath the root of a great fir-tree. Cotton-tail is counted among the good little bunnies—a characterization borne out by his actions throughout the tale. When their mother departed to gather supplies at the baker's, having left the four with firm instruction to avoid the dangerous garden of Mr. McGregor, Cotton-tail proved obedient where his brother Peter did not. Cotton-tail, alongside his siblings Flopsy and [[Mopsy]], went down the lane to gather blackberries as a lawful pastime, while Peter alone disobeyed and ventured into forbidden territory. After the day's misadventures befell the household, Cotton-tail enjoyed a proper supper of bread and milk with blackberries—the reward of good conduct—while Peter lay in bed, having been dosed with camomile tea by their mother as remedy for his transgression.

== Personality ==

Cotton-tail is a well-behaved rabbit, obedient and inclined toward virtue. She demonstrates good judgment and deference to parental authority, heeding her mother's instructions where others do not. Her temperament stands in marked contrast to her brother Peter's wayward nature, revealing a disposition governed by caution and propriety.

Cotton-tail shows an appetite for simple, honest pleasures. She takes contentment in lawful pursuits and modest fare, suggesting a character formed by restraint and domestic virtues. Her readiness to gather blackberries down the lane, rather than venture into forbidden territory, indicates both obedience and a sensible acceptance of the boundaries set for her protection.

== Appearance ==

Cotton-tail is one of four young rabbits living with their mother in a sand-bank beneath the root of a great fir-tree. Along with siblings Flopsy and Mopsy, Cotton-tail is counted among the good little bunnies of the household. When their mother ventured out to the baker's to purchase brown bread and currant buns, Cotton-tail and the other well-behaved siblings went down the lane to gather blackberries, whilst their brother Peter disobeyed and ran to Mr. McGregor's garden.

Later in the day, whilst Peter lay in bed recovering from his misadventure and receiving a dose of camomile tea from their mother, Cotton-tail joined Flopsy and Mopsy at supper, where they partook of bread and milk together with the blackberries they had gathered.

== Trivia ==

Cotton-tail is one of four rabbit siblings. Unlike his brother Peter, who disobeyed their mother's warnings and ventured into Mr. McGregor's garden, Cotton-tail demonstrated obedience and good behavior. On the afternoon when Peter met with misfortune, Cotton-tail joined his siblings Flopsy and Mopsy in gathering blackberries down the lane, and the three of them were described as good little bunnies. After Peter's harrowing escape and subsequent illness, Cotton-tail and Mopsy enjoyed bread and milk alongside blackberries for supper, whilst their brother remained in bed recovering from the effects of camomile tea.
